description: Public synthetic interoperability fixtures, not runtime implementation or provider qualification. Deterministic public TEST-ONLY seeds in scripts/publisher-attestation/generate.mjs must never protect real data. Decoded payloads, unsigned documents and cases are declarative generator inputs; derived keys, hashes, signed segments and transports are regenerated. Base positive is a fictional production Fastly declaration with provider checks not_assessed. Axum is development-only. No production provider method is qualified.
encoding: JWS signing input is ASCII protected_segment + dot + payload_segment. Verify those exact segments. JSON bytes use sorted keys and compact ASCII-compatible serialization; fixture values use the RFC 8785-compatible integer/ASCII subset. Digests of signed objects hash exact compact ASCII bytes.
validation_order: 1 bounded strict JSON/JWS decode with duplicate rejection
2 protected header, expected message type and trusted issuer key
4 payload schema and cross-field consistency, including per-check digest rules, message lifetimes, assessment observation intervals and the evidence key validity window
5 issuer, policy id/version/digest and method allowlists
6 exact evidence nonce comparison, then issuance skew, exclusive expiry and observation age
7 exact host, environment and binding equality with fresh evidence
8 result against the policy's required checks
10 independently known withdrawal/compromise, then live status when required
Verifier-issuance cases (operator authorization, durable state, signer fencing) are preconditions checked by the verifier, not consumer inputs.

harness.overrides: RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch against a fresh deep copy of external_context for every case. Arrays replace; null removes a member. Absent authority never authorizes a claimed identity; removed optional cache fields disable that cache behavior. Cases do not share caches or highest-seen sequences.
harness.inputs: Every signed case supplies expected_type independently of untrusted bytes. status_object selects a compact signed status; target_assessment selects the independently expected assessment for status-only cases. fresh_evidence selects the separately challenged response from signed_objects or negative_encodings; the generator uses collected_evidence for assessment evidence digests. Unsigned cases select unsigned_objects or negative_unsigned_objects. Evidence-only success is a self-declaration, not endorsement.
harness.stages: expected.stage is a number in validation_order. Evidence-only cases run stages 1–4, 6–7 and report self-declaration, not endorsement; assessment cases combine fresh evidence with stages 1–11. unsigned_admission uses decode/schema/key validation (1/4). verifier_issuance uses its separately numbered preconditions below. Success stage is the last completed stage. Cache cases use consumer stage 10 for status dependency invalidation. The bounded harness has one candidate issuer: threshold 1 accepts and thresholds above 1 reject. It does not test aggregation of several accepted issuers. Narrative scope is not an asserted harness output. Each consumer stage applies to the fresh evidence before the candidate assessment, so the first failing stage across both objects is reported.

verifier_issuance_stages.1: bounded decoding, schema, key admission and signature verification (malformed or signature_invalid)
verifier_issuance_stages.2: Active exact publisher/account/site authorization and optional operator authorization, with publication expiry caps (publisher_unauthorized/operator_unauthorized)
verifier_issuance_stages.3: durable authorization history and signer fencing (state_recovery_required)

harness.policy_documents: trusted_verifier.policy_documents contains the names of unsigned_objects policy documents pinned independently by id/version/digest. Evaluate those complete documents, not a consumer-local required_checks substitute.
